## Summary

<!-- What does this PR do, and why is it needed? State the affected layer(s). -->

- **Change type:** <!-- adapter / core CLI / setup+uninstall / shared config / docs -->
- **Layer(s):** <!-- L1 Setup · L2 Shared config · L3 Adapter · L4 Entry -->
- **Related issue:** <!-- #123, or "n/a — small fix" -->

## Universal checklist (always)

- [ ] The PR does a **single, focused** concern; unrelated changes are split out.
- [ ] `bash init/setup.sh` runs clean and is **idempotent** on a second run.
- [ ] `viseinit --all` reports every enabled adapter `[OK]` and exits `0`.
- [ ] `visectl doctor` reports all adapters OK.
- [ ] `git status --short` shows **no generated artifact** (`.vise/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`) — CONTRIBUTING §5.
- [ ] No contract in CONTRIBUTING §2 (C1–C12) is broken — flag it in the summary if a contract must change.
- [ ] Any **path/command/contract** change is accompanied by updated docs in the same PR (README / AGENTS.md / DESIGN.md / adapter README) — C12.

## If this PR adds or changes an adapter (L3)

- [ ] `vise.adapter.json` is complete: `schema_version`, `adapter_id` (unique), `name`, `version`, `description`, `required_cots`, `entry_points.cli`, `healthcheck`, `commands`.
- [ ] `commands` match the real CLI (no hidden args) — agents call them without `--help` probing.
- [ ] `init_steps` use the structured `run` + `args` form (C6).
- [ ] `thread` is idempotent and records any outside-`VISE_ROOT` write in the ledger (C9).
- [ ] `healthcheck` genuinely validates readiness and uses `$PYTHON` (not a bare `python`).
- [ ] `read` implemented if the adapter exposes knowledge; `provides` set where it categorizes a resource.
- [ ] Adapter `README.md` documents usage + the absolute-path/cwd caveat.
- [ ] Test points **T3.\*** run and pass (end-to-end self-test).

## If this PR touches the core CLI / behavior (L4)

- [ ] Exit codes (`0`–`6`) unchanged, or new codes documented (C3).
- [ ] `--json` output shape is stable for existing consumers; any breaking change is called out explicitly (C4).
- [ ] Every destructive action keeps a `--dry-run`/`preview` path.
- [ ] No implicit/silent execution introduced (no `PROMPT_COMMAND`, no always-on watcher) — C8, T7.1.
- [ ] `visectl run` cwd semantics unchanged (adapter directory) — C5.
- [ ] Test points **T2.\*** and **T5.\*** (if scheduling) run and pass.

## If this PR touches setup / shell integration / uninstall (L1)

- [ ] rc injection stays idempotent and marker-exact (`# >>> Vise >>>` / `# <<< Vise <<<`) — C10.
- [ ] Both `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc` are handled.
- [ ] Any write outside `VISE_ROOT` is recorded in the ledger; wrappers keep the `# Auto-generated by` header — C9.
- [ ] `bash init/uninstall.sh --dry-run` accounts for everything the PR adds (verified in a sandbox — T6).
- [ ] No `sed -i` / PowerShell; file edits use Python — C11, T8.

## If this PR touches shared config / path resolution (L2)

- [ ] Schema separation preserved: `core/adapter_paths.json` nested (hand-maintained) vs `.vise/tool_paths.json` flat (generated).
- [ ] `PATH` fallback still works when a tool path is unset; version checks still enforced.
- [ ] Test points **T4.\*** run and pass.

## If this is docs-only

- [ ] No code or generated artifact changed (`git status --short` shows only `*.md`).
- [ ] Every command shown exists; relative links resolve — T9.
